scope: The five employers v6 left UNRESOLVED, plus PureHealth, whose v6 MANUAL_LINK depended on reading its homepage after robots.txt answered with a Cloudflare 403. Research only: no source was added, enabled or fetched through ASTRA, no job-listing API was called, no form was submitted and no e-mail was sent.

tool_note: Both logs were produced by scripts/source_route_check.py at commit e5e5725e95719d13a849b639584af917158d4891 (git blob e3f0a31b041a63f6cbc67a444952599d3b4e4c2b), as each log records. Later commits changed its module docstring, made four behaviour changes, none of which alters a v7 classification, and added one explicit hardening. (1) A robots.txt 3xx without a usable (missing, empty or blank) Location now ends the robots check after one request. The tool at e5e5725 did not log the Location header and would have logged such an answer as a redirect to its own URL, so the logs cannot show whether this case arose. Three of the seven 3xx answers name a different target; the four later HCT robots hops are logged as redirecting to themselves, which v4 also recorded as a self-redirect. Either way the HCT robots decision is the same: disallow all. (2) A page 3xx with a blank Location now records redirect_error instead of its own URL; this did not arise, because the one page 3xx (DoH /en/careers) named a different target. (3) A blank href is now skipped as unusable instead of becoming a link to the page itself; no logged page contains such a self-link. (4) A follow-on step whose source step was not requested now says so. Change 4 affects how six existing log entries read: the five "no link from ... matched" entries (three in the main log, two in the follow-up log) and "zu-careers-host did not redirect" all belong to follow-on steps whose source step was not requested, and nothing was requested for them. (5) The verified handshake of the TLS diagnostic now sets TLS 1.2 as its minimum explicitly, following CodeQL alert py/insecure-protocol; the unverified certificate-date read keeps Python's own default. On the Python that ran v7 (3.13.2, OpenSSL 3.0.15) both already had a TLS 1.2 minimum, so the v7 diagnostics are unaffected.
rules: Every request was made from the Owner's machine by scripts/source_route_check.py at the tool commit above, with the v5/v6 User-Agent. The raw logs are the tool's own output, committed unchanged.

Pacing: at least 2 seconds between contacts with one host (HTTP requests and TLS handshakes), counted from the end of the previous contact to the start of the next. The logs record every start and end time in milliseconds; every same-host interval in both runs was at least 2.000 s. This is a v7 result only. The v6 log does not establish its intended minimum, and nothing here changes that.

robots.txt per RFC 9309, compared after section 2.2.2 normalisation on the exact path sent. 404 and other 4xx answers mean robots is unavailable (allowed), except 401, 403 and 429. Those, 5xx, a network or TLS failure, a bot-protection page, HTML served as robots.txt, a 3xx without a usable redirect and more than five redirects all mean disallow all.

Page redirects were never followed automatically (robots.txt redirects were followed, paced and logged, up to five hops, as RFC 9309 expects), no cookie was kept or sent, and login, apply, registration and account URLs and hosts were refused. A bot-protection page on any request blocked that host for the rest of the run. Certificates were verified for every HTTP request and for the verified handshake of the TLS diagnostic. After that handshake failed, one separate diagnostic handshake read aderp.abudhabi.ae's presented certificate without verification, only to report its dates; it sent no HTTP request and nothing from the host was used.

Officialness: the employer's own domain, or an ATS the employer's own page links or redirects to. ATS branding and company profiles alone stay unverified leads. Whether an employer-published link to a third-party jobs search counts is an open Owner decision.
DNS steps resolved conventional careers hostnames on the employer's own domain without contacting them. The one that resolved was followed up by a separate, recorded plan.
rule_changes_disclosed: v4 treated a Cloudflare 403 at robots.txt as "do not fetch this host". Its PureHealth record says that continuing would mean working around bot protection. v5 and v6 instead read the same response as RFC 9309 "unavailable, allowed". v6 stated that 4xx rule, but neither record said it reversed v4's treatment. PureHealth's v6 MANUAL_LINK was obtained that way. So were v5's two Emirates Islamic careers-page requests (06:13:16 and 06:13:18Z), v6's two Emirates Islamic page requests and v6's read of the talentone.ae homepage (13:43:12Z). The Emirates Islamic requests were all answered with Cloudflare pages, none was bypassed, and no classification rests on the talentone.ae read. v7 restores the v4 rule. No Owner decision authorised the v5/v6 reading.

v7 blocks a host for the rest of the run after any bot-protection page. v4 to v6 stopped only the challenged path; v4 itself read another ADPHC path after a path-level rejection. ADPHC's v6 MANUAL_LINK is therefore consistent with the v4 rule and is not reopened.
HCT: the conservative reading of more than five robots redirects is unchanged. RFC 9309 would permit reading it as "unavailable"; that remains an Owner decision and is not relaxed here.
counts_note: v6 had 0 / 50 / 5. PureHealth returns to UNRESOLVED; the other five stay UNRESOLVED. No new supported feed was verified. The SMARTRECRUITERS_OWNER_DECISION count stays 0 as recorded in v4, although Masdar and Etihad Airways match that outcome's definition; reclassifying them belongs to the Owner's SmartRecruiters decision (see the source map).
scan: No new permitted Greenhouse, Lever or Ashby feed was verified, so no controlled scan scope was prepared, ASTRA was not started, and run 107 was not repeated.
not_claimed: No posting is claimed open, and no row is covered automatically.
A MANUAL_LINK is a link for the user to open; ASTRA does not read it.
The nine-source controlled scan (run 107) neither covers nor validates any of these employers.

errata: v5 (kept unchanged): the PureHealth evidence says "the one careers request". Its log shows three careers-path requests (06:13:01, 06:13:05 and 06:13:06Z). v5 logged only the robots.txt 403; v4 recorded the same response as a Cloudflare block page and v6 and v7 logged a Cloudflare page, so bot protection was most likely met, though not bypassed.
v5 (kept unchanged): the DoH 404 page after /en/careers is labelled "bot_protection". That was a classifier false positive; it is an ordinary not-found page, as v4 and v6 recorded.
v6 (kept unchanged): "The presented certificate (GlobalSign RSA OV SSL CA 2018) expired" names the issuing CA. The certificate that expired is the leaf for aderp.abudhabi.ae, issued by that CA.
v6 (kept unchanged): its request log does not establish the intended two-second same-host minimum. The v6 script stamped each entry before its wait, to the second. v7 does not change that finding.

The Emirates Islamic "later independent access check" added to the source map with v6 (robots.txt HTTP 200 with an HTML page) was not logged with a time, URL or status. v7 logged robots.txt answering 403 with a Cloudflare bot-protection page. Access varies, and the row stays UNRESOLVED either way.
